A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SIMECO shape-completion work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original PCN, KITTI, and OmniObject3D experiments, alongside architectural ablations, robustness tests, and computational analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a VN-SPD ablation, training-convergence comparisons, and a thin-structure subset analysis.

M1.justification: The architecture, canonicalization, attention, transform restoration, and training objective are unchanged. The VN-SPD constraint tested in the new ablation was already specified through the linear-weight constraint in v1 Appendix C.2, Equation 12.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same shape-completion task on PCN, KITTI, and OmniObject3D. The new thin-structure analysis selects 50 cases from the existing 1,200-case test set; it adds a subgroup analysis without introducing new data or input conditions.

E2.justification: v3 Table 7 adds a centered SIMECO comparator using standard VN layers with partial-input centering and normalization. The external baseline membership in the existing benchmark, latency, and parameter-budget comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds the centered-model control and a defined subset-selection procedure: local PCA over 30 nearest neighbors, selecting shapes where more than 0.5% of points have anisotropy above 0.8. Existing benchmark transforms, metrics, and the 200-epoch training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds targeted checks of the VN-SPD constraint, training convergence against AdaPoinTr, and performance on thin-structure cases. These extend the existing ablation and efficiency analyses; the earlier normalization, capacity, robustness, and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 11 retains category-wise min–max shading, and the new convergence curves introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds centered-SIMECO results of 9.31 CD-ℓ1 and 0.673 F1, versus the retained full-model values of 8.59 and 0.714. It also reports approximately 50 versus 140 epochs to reach CD-ℓ1 below 10 and CD-ℓ1 of 6.83 on the thin-structure subset. Existing results are unchanged; 6.83 versus 8.59 compares different sample populations.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly defines the local PCA score L = (σ1 − σ2)/σ1 for identifying thin structures. This is a limited mathematical-definition addition for the empirical analysis. The SIM(3) definitions, propositions, proofs, and approximate-equivariance discussion in Appendix C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about alignment bias, the first SIM(3)-equivariant completion architecture, the de-biased protocol, and synthetic-to-real generalization. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation that VN-SPD learns a center rather than fixing it, interpreting this as more principled optimization. It also interprets the thin-subset result as evidence of effective detail preservation. The existing applicability limitations and failure explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 describes the centered control and gives the PCA neighborhood size and filtering thresholds for reproducing the new subset analysis. The acknowledgment newly identifies the source of pretrained ESCAPE weights. Existing code-access information, optimizer settings, hardware, and training budget are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 64 cited works and the same related-work positioning are retained. VN-SPD refers to work already credited for the linear constraint in v1. Reference edits concern bibliographic formatting and metadata rather than added literature or changed novelty claims.

P1.justification: v3 adds two Appendix B subsections and expands the computational-efficiency discussion while preserving the main narrative. Limited editorial changes include the NeurIPS 2025 publication footer, corresponding-author wording, acknowledgments, and bibliography cleanup.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 7 and the four-panel convergence Figure 12. Existing appendix tables and figures are renumbered and reflowed, and the extended cross-domain figure gains a missing GT column heading. The main-text displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new VN-SPD control and epoch-wise convergence curves provide useful evidence for architectural choices and optimization behavior that v1 lacked. The gain is limited: the principal results and theory are unchanged, and the thin-structure analysis uses whole-shape error on a selected subset without a matched baseline, so it provides only limited evidence about thin-part reconstruction.
